theory.intro: Data can be shown in a table, a column graph or a line graph. You can read single values and also combine them to find totals.
facts: A **table** lists each category with its value; a **column graph** shows each value as a bar height.
To find a **total**, add the values of all categories together.
Always check the scale of a graph — one step may be worth more than $1$.
steps: Read the value for each category from the table or bar height.
For a total, add every value together.
For a difference, subtract the smaller value from the larger.

workedExamples.question_text:
The table shows books borrowed from a school library.

| Day | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Books | 24 | 36 | 18 | 32 |

(a) How many books were borrowed on Tuesday?
(b) How many books were borrowed altogether?
(c) How many more books were borrowed on Tuesday than on Wednesday?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Read the Tuesday column: $36$ books.

(b) Add all four values.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}24+36+18+32\\&=110\end{aligned}$
Altogether, $110$ books were borrowed.

(c) Subtract Wednesday's value from Tuesday's value.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}36-18\\&=18\end{aligned}$
Tuesday had $18$ more books borrowed.

workedExamples.question_text:
A class collected $100$ cans altogether. How many cans did the Green group collect?

| Group | Red | Blue | Green | Yellow |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cans | 23 | 28 | ? | 19 |
workedExamples.solution_text:
Add the three known values.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}23+28+19\\&=70\end{aligned}$

Subtract this subtotal from the total.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}100-70\\&=30\end{aligned}$

The Green group collected $30$ cans.

(a) Each vertical scale step represents $5$ requests. The Art column reaches $15$, so Art had $15$ requests.

(b) Sport has the tallest column: $25$ requests. Music has a value of $0$, so Music had the fewest requests.

(c) Art had $15$ requests and Chess had $10$. Art had more requests.

(d) Read Sport as $25$ and Chess as $10$, then subtract.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}25-10\\&=15\end{aligned}$
Sport had $15$ more requests than Chess.

foundation.question_text:
The table shows visitors to community rooms.
How many visited the Games room?
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Room}&\text{Craft}&\text{Games}&\text{Study}&\text{Music}\\\hline\text{Visitors}&18&27&14&21\end{array}$

Find the total number of meals delivered.
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Day}&\text{Mon}&\text{Tue}&\text{Wed}&\text{Thu}\\\hline\text{Meals}&32&28&35&25\end{array}$

foundation.solution_text:
The West bar is the tallest.
West had the most volunteer shifts.

foundation.question_text:
How many more parcels did Route B deliver than Route D?
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Route}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Parcels}&45&62&38&27\end{array}$

foundation.solution_text:
The point at $11$ a.m. is at $15$.
$15\text{ calls}$

development.question_text:
The total attendance was $150$.
Find the missing Friday value.
$\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}\text{Day}&\text{Mon}&\text{Tue}&\text{Wed}&\text{Thu}&\text{Fri}\\\hline\text{Attendance}&26&31&29&34&?\end{array}$

development.solution_text:
Garden has $40$ members and Sports has $50$ members.
Sports has more members.

development.question_text:
A food bank packed $184$ boxes in total.
Use the table to find how many were Vegetable boxes.
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Box type}&\text{Fruit}&\text{Dry}&\text{Chilled}&\text{Vegetable}\\\hline\text{Boxes}&46&58&35&?\end{array}$

development.solution_text:
Clinic C has $120$ visits and Clinic D has $60$ visits.
$120-60$
$=60\text{ visits}$

development.question_text:
A transport desk records enquiries.
How many more train enquiries were made in the morning than in the afternoon?
$\begin{array}{c|rrr} &\text{Bus}&\text{Train}&\text{Ferry}\\\hline\text{Morning}&24&31&15\\\text{Afternoon}&18&27&20\end{array}$

development.solution_text:
Legal received $0$ requests.
Legal received the fewest requests.

mastery.question_text:
The table shows the number of enquiries received by four centres.
The total was $375$. Find the missing value.
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Centre}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Enquiries}&86&97&78&?\end{array}$

The table shows deliveries to five centres.
How many more deliveries did Centre E receive than Centre C?
$\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}\text{Centre}&A&B&C&D&E\\\hline\text{Deliveries}&145&175&138&160&192\end{array}$

The table shows bookings for four workshops.
There were $425$ bookings in total. Find the missing value.
$\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Workshop}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Bookings}&118&96&127&?\end{array}$
